title: 3.6.12 Lab: Object-Parameter Mutation
description: Mutate a property on an object parameter and prove the caller sees it, then write a non-mutating version that keeps the original untouched. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Define a function that mutates a property
steps.instructions: Define a function (the lesson calls it birthday; name it for what you are building) that takes one object parameter and adds 1 to its age property. Do not reassign the parameter; change the property the object already has.

steps.title: Call it and log the caller's object
steps.instructions: Create an object variable (the lesson calls it user; name it for what you are building) with a name and an age. Call birthday with it, then console.log the caller's object. Confirm the age changed, because objects pass as a reference.

steps.title: Write a non-mutating version
steps.instructions: Define a second function (the lesson calls it birthdaySafe; name it for what you are building) that returns a new object with the age increased, without changing the object it was given. Call it and log both the original and the returned object to prove the original is untouched. Write the changed property after the spread, like { ...person, age: 31 }. Make the copy with spread.

requirements.title: birthday defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named birthday. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: Define a function (the lesson calls it birthday; name it for what you are building) with one parameter, the person object.

requirements.title: property mutated
requirements.description: Code assigns to a property on the parameter object. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: Change a property the object already has by assigning to it, such as person.age. Do not point the parameter at a new object.

requirements.title: birthdaySafe defined
requirements.description: Code defines a function named birthdaySafe. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Define a second function (the lesson calls it birthdaySafe; name it for what you are building) that also takes one object.

requirements.title: object spread used
requirements.description: Code copies the object with spread syntax. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Copy the object with spread in braces, then write the changed property after it, so the original is not touched.

requirements.title: results logged
requirements.description: Code calls console.log. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: birthday raises the age on the object it is given
requirements.description: birthday({ name: "A", age: 10 }) leaves that same object with age 11. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: birthday must change the age property of the object it receives: person.age = person.age + 1. Do not return a new object here.

requirements.title: birthdaySafe returns an older copy and leaves the original alone
requirements.description: birthdaySafe({ name: "A", age: 10 }) returns { name: "A", age: 11 } and the object passed in still has age 10. Help: 3.6.9 (Side Effects and Copies)
requirements.hint: Build and return a new object ({ ...person, age: person.age + 1 }). Never assign to a property of the object you were given.

requirements.title: the caller's object is printed after the call
requirements.description: user holds a name and an age, and the printed output shows both the name and the age user ends with. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: Call birthday(user), then print user itself so its new age shows in the output.

checks.expr: user !== null && typeof user === 'object' && typeof user.name === 'string' && typeof user.age === 'number' && (J => J.includes(user.name) && J.includes(String(user.age)))(output.join(' '))
checks.fail: user should hold a name and an age, and you should print user after calling birthday so its new age shows.

requirements.title: birthday called
requirements.description: Code calls birthday. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: Define birthday, then call it: birthday(...). A function nobody calls changes nothing.

requirements.title: birthdaySafe called
requirements.description: Code calls birthdaySafe. Help: 3.6.10 (Defensive Copying: [...] and {...})
requirements.hint: Define birthdaySafe, then call it: birthdaySafe(...). A function nobody calls changes nothing.

requirements.title: the user object is printed by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints the name or age of user, or the whole object. Help: 3.6.5 (Changing vs. Reassigning)
requirements.hint: Print the caller's data with a console.log that runs. Typed-in text, or a print that never runs, does not count.

checks.fail: Print user (its name and age, or the whole object) with console.log calls that run, after birthday and after birthdaySafe. Typed text does not count.
